findings.title: Referer-based host check is trivially bypassable and inconsistent with embeddable_host semantics
findings.body: ensure_embeddable compares URI(request.referer).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host with exact string equality. The Referer header is fully client-controlled, so any site can send a forged Referer matching embeddable_host and load the embed endpoint in an iframe. Additionally, embeddable_host is documented as 'Host that can embed the comments from this Discourse forum' (a single host), but the check requires an exact host match with no subdomain handling, and a blank referer yields URI('').host == nil which fails closed only by accident. The endpoint also sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL, which is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive value (valid values are DENY and SAMEORIGIN), so browsers ignore it and framing is unrestricted. The real protection is the referer check, which is spoofable; combined with the fact that the action enqueues a server-side fetch (Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...)) of an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL, this allows an attacker to make the Discourse server issue requests to arbitrary hosts (SSRF) by embedding the iframe with a forged Referer. The embed_url is later fetched by TopicRetriever/TopicEmbed.import_remote via open(url).

findings.title: Arbitrary embed_url triggers server-side fetch of attacker-controlled URL (SSRF)
findings.body: The best action takes params[:embed_url] with no validation and enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: embed_url). RetrieveTopic passes it to TopicRetriever, which only checks that URI(embed_url).host equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host. An attacker who controls any page on the embeddable host (or can spoof the Referer as noted above) can supply embed_url values pointing at internal addresses (e.g. http://embeddable_host@169.254.169.254/... or URLs whose host string matches but resolve internally, or simply use the embeddable host as a proxy to fetch internal paths). TopicEmbed.import_remote then calls open(url).read, causing the server to fetch and parse the response, and the fetched content is stored as a post. There is no scheme restriction beyond the implicit http(s) of open-uri, no blocklist of private IP ranges, and no restriction on ports. This is a server-side request forgery vector that also creates topics from the fetched content.

findings.title: Imported RSS/feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization (stored XSS)
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends an 'imported from' footer to the feed-supplied contents and creates the post with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. In app/models/post.rb, cook returns raw unchanged when cook_method == raw_html, bypassing the entire Markdown rendering/sanitization pipeline (PrettyText/cook normally sanitizes HTML). The resulting post.cooked is then rendered in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19 with <%= raw post.cooked %>, and also rendered normally elsewhere in the forum. The content comes from an RSS/ATOM feed (Jobs::PollFeed passes i.content through CGI.unescapeHTML) or from an arbitrary fetched page (import_remote via ruby-readability, which whitelists only a few tags/attributes but still passes through and including javascript: URLs potentially, and import() is also called directly with unsanitized content). findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string in place
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import does contents << "\n<hr>..." which mutates the String object passed by the caller. In Jobs::PollFeed, content is built per item so impact is limited, but in TopicEmbed.import_remote, doc.content is passed and mutated; more importantly the content_sha1 is computed AFTER the mutation (line 16), which is consistent, but any caller that reuses the same string across calls (e.g. computing its own hash beforehand, or the Disqus thor task) will see the string changed. This is a hidden side effect that can corrupt data or cause incorrect change detection (content_sha1 comparisons) for callers that pre-compute hashes. The method should dup the string before appending.

findings.title: URL validation regex is too permissive and inconsistent with the rest of the code
findings.body: The guard `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` accepts URLs like 'http://' followed by anything, including 'http://<script>' or 'http:///path', and does not reject whitespace/control characters. Elsewhere the codebase uses the same loose pattern (poll_feed.rb line 33, topic_retriever invalid_host?), but TopicEmbed.import is the final gate before open(url) and post creation. A URL such as 'http://example.com/\nSet-Cookie: ...' or one containing spaces can be passed to open-uri. More importantly, the regex does not anchor the end and allows e.g. 'http://host\t.evil.com' style tricks depending on URI parsing differences between the regex check and URI()/open-uri. A stricter validation (URI.parse with scheme whitelist and host presence) should be used before the URL is fetched or stored.

findings.title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URL with open() and no redirect/size limits
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout, no redirect limit, no content-size limit, and no scheme/IP restrictions. Combined with the SSRF surface described in the controller finding, a malicious embed_url can cause the Sidekiq worker to hang indefinitely (no timeout on open-uri), follow redirects to internal hosts, or download unbounded content into memory (read with no limit) causing memory exhaustion. ruby-readability then parses the entire document. At minimum open-uri timeouts (open(url, read_timeout:, open_timeout:) or a redirect cap and maximum body size) should be enforced.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes the whole job when the feed is unreachable or malformed; no error handling and feed_key is dead code
findings.body: poll_feed calls SimpleRSS.parse(open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)) with no rescue. If the feed URL is down, returns invalid XML, or open-uri raises (SocketError, Errno::ECONNREFUSED, OpenURI::HTTPError, etc.), the exception propagates out of execute. The job is declared sidekiq_options retry: false, so a single transient failure permanently skips that run (until the next hourly recurrence) and, worse, any items already processed in the loop before the exception are committed (TopicEmbed.import runs per item with its own transaction) while the rest are lost — there is no per-item error isolation either, so one bad item (e.g. i.content being nil causing NoMethodError on .scrub at line 35) aborts processing of all remaining items. Additionally, feed_key (lines 20-22) is defined but never used anywhere, indicating intended caching/last-modified logic was never wired up. The job should rescue per-item errors, rescue overall fetch errors, and use feed_key or remove it.

findings.title: i.content can be nil causing NoMethodError; i.link/i.id handling is fragile
findings.body: Line 35 calls i.content.scrub without a nil check. SimpleRSS items frequently have nil content (e.g. RSS 2.0 items with only a description, or Atom entries without content), which raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire poll_feed loop as described above. Similarly i.title can be nil and is passed to TopicEmbed.import as the topic title, which will fail topic title validation (though skip_validations: true is set, downstream TopicCreator may still misbehave) or produce a broken topic. The code should guard with i.content.to_s and fall back to i.description, and handle missing titles.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses indexOf (substring match) allowing origin spoofing
findings.body: The handler validates the message origin with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. indexOf performs a substring check, not an origin comparison: an attacker page at https://evil.com/?x=discourseUrl-value or at a host containing the discourse URL as a substring (e.g. https://discourse.example.com.evil.com when discourseUrl is https://discourse.example.com) will pass the check because e.origin contains the discourseUrl string. The correct check is to compare against the parsed origin of discourseUrl (e.g. new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin). Because the handler sets iframe.height from e.data.height, a spoofed message can resize the iframe arbitrarily (UI redress / covering page content). The iframe src is also constructed from discourseEmbedUrl which is attacker-influenced via the embedding page, but the origin check flaw is the concrete bug here.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is the raw Referer header, enabling message leak to attacker-controlled origins
findings.body: The layout sends the resize message with `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The targetOrigin is the full Referer URL string, not an origin. Per the postMessage spec, if targetOrigin is not '*' or '/', it must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]); a full URL with a path is compared as a string prefix against the parent's origin, so 'http://eviltrout.com/some/page' will NOT match the parent origin 'http://eviltrout.com' and the message will silently not be delivered (functional bug), but more importantly the value is derived from the client-controlled Referer header. If an attacker can get the iframe loaded with a crafted Referer (or the referer is an attacker-influenced URL), the height data is posted to that origin. The targetOrigin should be derived server-side from SiteSetting.embeddable_host (the validated host), not from request.referer. Also note request.referer is interpolated into a JS string literal without escaping — a Referer containing a quote would break out of the string (though browsers constrain header characters, it is still incorrect to interpolate unescaped).

findings.title: Unescaped attribute interpolation for avatar URL and username
findings.body: Line 16 uses `` with raw ERB interpolation inside a single-quoted HTML attribute, and line 17 outputs `<%= post.user.username %>` (this one is escaped by default, fine). small_avatar_url is generally a Discourse-generated URL, but if it is nil (user without avatar) the src becomes empty; more importantly, interpolating into an attribute without the asset/URL helpers and without escaping is fragile — a URL containing a single quote would break out of the attribute. The codebase convention is to use double-quoted attributes with standard <%= %> escaping (which escapes quotes as "). This should be ``.

findings.title: raw post.cooked renders unsanitized HTML in the embed iframe (stored XSS sink)
findings.body: Line 19 renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. For posts created via TopicEmbed.import, cooked is the raw feed HTML because cook_method raw_html bypasses sanitization (see post.rb finding). Even for normal cooked posts, Discourse's cooked HTML is sanitized for the main app, but the embed view is a separate, minimal layout; rendering raw cooked here means any content that survived (or bypassed) sanitization is rendered in the iframe. Combined with the raw_html import path, this is the sink that turns feed-controlled HTML into executed script in the forum origin. The embed view should render cooked through the same sanitization guarantees as the main app (which it nominally does for regular posts) and must never render raw_html-cooked posts without sanitization; at minimum, posts with cook_method raw_html should be sanitized before display.

findings.title: cook_method raw_html bypasses all cooking/sanitization for post content
findings.body: The new cook method returns raw verbatim when cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], skipping post_analyzer.cook which is where Markdown rendering and HTML sanitization (via Sanitize) occur. Any code path that sets cook_method to raw_html (TopicEmbed.import, and the Disqus thor task which sets cooked directly) therefore stores completely unsanitized HTML in the cooked column. cooked is treated as trusted, pre-sanitized HTML throughout Discourse (rendered with raw in many views, used in excerpts, feeds, emails, and the new embed view). There is no compensating sanitization anywhere on this path. This is a stored-XSS primitive: whoever can influence content imported via RSS/feed or Disqus import controls cooked HTML rendered to all users. The raw_html path must sanitize (e.g. with Sanitize using Discourse's whitelist) before storing, or the feature should be removed.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import creates topics with skip_validations: true, bypassing title/post validation and spam checks
findings.body: PostCreator.new is called with skip_validations: true, which disables post validation (save(validate: false) in PostCreator#save_post) and skips SpamRulesEnforcer (PostCreator#create only enforces spam rules when !@opts[:skip_validations]). Feed-supplied titles (which can be nil, empty, extremely long, or contain control characters) and feed-supplied raw content therefore bypass min/max title length, min post length, max post length, and all spam rules. This allows the feed to create malformed topics (e.g. nil/empty title, oversized posts exceeding max_post_length) and to spam the forum with content that would normally be rejected. The import path should validate titles and enforce length limits, or at minimum sanitize/truncate the title and enforce max_post_length.

findings.title: PostRevisor.revise! with skip_validations can fail silently and leaves embed.content_sha1 updated even if revision failed
findings.body: In the update branch, revisor.revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true) is called and its return value is ignored. PostRevisor#revise! returns false when the raw hasn't changed (should_revise?) and update_post calls @post.save(validate: false) whose failure is not checked (save returns false but no exception, and revise! still returns true). After this, embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) unconditionally updates the stored hash. If the revision failed to persist (validation skipped but a DB constraint failed, or save returned false), the embed now claims the new content_sha1 while the post still holds the old content, so future polls will never detect the change again (permanent divergence). The return value of revise! should be checked and the sha1 update should happen only on success, ideally inside the same transaction.

findings.title: Check-then-create race on embed_url allows duplicate topics despite unique index
findings.body: import does TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and then, if blank, creates a topic/post/TopicEmbed inside a transaction. There is a TOCTOU race: two concurrent imports (e.g. PollFeed running hourly plus RetrieveTopic jobs triggered by embed requests, or multiple Sidekiq workers) can both observe embed.blank? and both create topics. The unique index on embed_url (migration 20131217174004) will cause the second TopicEmbed.create! to raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, rolling back the second transaction — but the first transaction may have already committed, so the net effect is an exception in the job (which for PollFeed has retry: false, so it's lost) and potentially confusing partial behavior. The code should rely on the unique index (rescue RecordNotUnique and re-read) or use a unique constraint check at creation time rather than a pre-check.

findings.title: Host validation compares embeddable_host to URI host with exact equality, no scheme/port normalization
findings.body: invalid_host? returns true unless SiteSetting.embeddable_host == URI(@embed_url).host. This means an embed_url of 'http://embeddable_host:8080/x' or 'https://embeddable_host/x' passes as long as the host string matches, and more importantly the check does not restrict the scheme — 'file://embeddable_host/...' would have host 'embeddable_host'? (URI('file://embeddable_host/etc/passwd').host is 'embeddable_host'), and open-uri supports file:// URLs, so TopicEmbed.import_remote's open(url) could read local files if a file:// URL with matching host passes. Actually open-uri does support file:// ; URI('file://embeddable_host/etc/passwd').host == 'embeddable_host' so invalid_host? is false and the file would be fetched and imported. The validation must whitelist the scheme (http/https only) and ideally normalize/compare ports.

findings.title: Throttle key uses raw embed_url in Redis key without namespacing/escaping
findings.body: retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" interpolates the full URL into a Redis key. URLs can contain characters that are legal in Redis keys but make keys unbounded in length (Redis keys can be up to 512MB, but very long keys waste memory) and there is no collision-safety concern here since the full URL is the key. More relevantly, the throttle is per-URL and setnx+expire is not atomic with the subsequent work: if the process crashes after setnx but before perform_retrieve completes, the URL is throttled for 60s with no topic created, and the embed shows 'loading' until the next request after expiry. This is acceptable behavior, but the key should be hashed (e.g. Digest::SHA1) to bound key size, consistent with feed_key's approach in poll_feed.rb.

findings.title: no_throttle is set from user.try(:staff?) but the user lookup can return nil and the throttle bypass applies to any staff user id passed in args
findings.body: The job accepts args[:user_id] from the enqueued args and looks up the user; if that user is staff, no_throttle is true, disabling the 60-second retrieval throttle. The controller passes current_user.try(:id), so a staff user browsing the embed repeatedly bypasses throttling — that's intended. However, the job trusts args[:user_id] without verifying the requester is actually that user (jobs are enqueued server-side so this is fine in the current call path), but the RetrieveTopic job is a regular (non-scheduled) job that any code path can enqueue with an arbitrary user_id; combined with the SSRF surface, a staff user_id disables throttling for arbitrary URL fetches. This is a minor trust-boundary note; the main issue is that the throttle bypass is keyed off a user-supplied id in a job payload.

findings.title: TopicView.new is called with current_user which may be nil, and no topic access check is performed
findings.body: When a topic_id is found, the controller builds TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) and renders the posts in best.html.erb. current_user is nil for anonymous iframe requests (the embed is loaded cross-site in an iframe where cookies may not be sent depending on browser settings). More importantly, there is no check that the topic is publicly visible: TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns any topic id for the URL, including topics in restricted categories, private messages, or deleted/hidden topics. TopicView with an anonymous user normally filters posts by guardian permissions, but the embed controller does not verify the topic is accessible to anonymous users, and the embed view renders post.cooked, usernames, and avatar URLs directly. If an embed_url maps to a topic in a restricted category (e.g. via feed import misconfiguration or a leaked URL), the embed endpoint leaks its content to anyone who knows the embed_url. The controller should verify the topic is visible to anonymous users (e.g. guardian.can_see?(topic) with anonymous user) before rendering.

findings.title: discourse_expires_in 1.minute caches the loading page and topic view for anonymous users without varying on embed_url
findings.body: The action sets discourse_expires_in 1.minute, which sets a short public cache TTL. The response content depends entirely on the embed_url query parameter. If a shared/CDN cache caches the response without including the query string in the cache key (or if the framework's expires_in sets Cache-Control: public), one user's embed_url response could be served to another user requesting a different embed_url, leaking topic content across embed URLs. Rails' discourse_expires_in typically sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=60 with no Vary on the query param. The response should be marked private/no-cache (the content is per-URL and per-user), or at minimum Vary on the embed_url parameter.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever to be used directly, but the controller enqueues a job instead
findings.body: The test 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' sets TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever) and retriever.expects(:retrieve), then performs get :best. But the controller code calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) — it never instantiates TopicRetriever. This test would fail against the actual implementation (TopicRetriever.new is never called), meaning the spec does not match the code and provides false confidence. Either the controller should call TopicRetriever directly (synchronously) or the spec should expect Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) with the right args. As written, the test suite is broken/misleading for this behavior.

findings.title: Spec asserts exact HTML serialization that depends on Nokogiri version behavior
findings.body: The test asserts post.cooked.start_with?("hello world new post hello ") — an exact string match on Nokogiri's fragment.to_html output (attribute quoting, tag self-closing style, attribute order). Nokogiri's HTML serialization is not guaranteed stable across versions (e.g. libxml2 version differences change attribute quoting and void-element serialization), so this test is brittle and can fail for reasons unrelated to the code under test. It should assert on parsed structure (e.g. Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(post.cooked).at_css('a')['href']) instead of exact string prefix matching.

findings.title: Migration uses force: true which drops an existing table
findings.body: create_table :topic_embeds, force: true will DROP the table if it already exists, destroying all data. The companion migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb was also changed to add force: true. Using force: true in a migration is dangerous: if this migration is ever run on a database where the table already exists (e.g. re-running after a partial failure, or on a restored backup), it silently destroys all topic_embeds/top_topics data. Migrations should be idempotent without force, or use create_table ... unless table_exists?. The change to add force: true to the existing create_top_topics migration is an unrelated and risky modification.

findings.title: Disqus import rewritten to use TopicEmbed.import_remote but reply posts are created with raw HTML cooked and no cook_method, breaking rendering
findings.body: The import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]) to create the topic, then creates reply posts with attrs = { topic_id:, raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked], created_at: } via PostCreator.new(post_user, attrs).create. The Disqus export's p[:cooked] is HTML (from the Disqus message field). Setting cooked directly while raw is also HTML means the post's raw is HTML treated as Markdown source; on any later edit/revision, Post#cook will run the Markdown pipeline over HTML, and the before_save callback (post.rb line 321: self.cooked = cook(raw, ...) unless new_record?) will re-cook on update, mangling the HTML. Also, unlike the topic post (which gets cook_method raw_html via import), these reply posts have default cook_method regular, so cooked and raw diverge and the stored cooked is unsanitized HTML rendered with raw elsewhere — the same stored-XSS issue as the feed import, plus content corruption on edit. The reply posts should either be created with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] (and sanitized) or, preferably, with raw set to the HTML and cooked left to be generated by the normal pipeline after sanitization.

findings.title: Disqus import creates users with User.create! without password/username validation and can create duplicate/spam accounts
findings.body: For each Disqus post with an author_email, the importer does User.where(email: email).first and, if missing, User.create!(email: email, username: UserNameSuggester.suggest(email)). This creates forum accounts for arbitrary email addresses found in a Disqus export, without activation, without trust level restrictions, and with auto-generated usernames. Combined with the fact that these users' posts are created with the unsanitized cooked HTML, this both pollutes the user table (unactivated accounts that count toward stats, can be emailed, appear in user lists depending on settings) and amplifies the XSS issue. The importer should use a single designated user (options[:post_as]) for all replies, or create users via the proper signup/approval flow, and should not create accounts from untrusted export data.

findings.title: URL fallback regex allows non-http schemes to be treated as valid item URLs
findings.body: url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\// — when the link is blank or not http(s), the code falls back to i.id, which for Atom feeds is often a URN (e.g. 'urn:uuid:...') or an arbitrary string. TopicEmbed.import then rejects it (returns nil unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//), so the item is silently skipped — but the intent appears to be to use i.id as a fallback URL, which will almost never be a valid http URL. This means Atom feeds whose entries lack a proper <link href> are silently dropped. The fallback is ineffective; the code should skip items without a valid http(s) link rather than passing a URN to import.

findings.title: Script assumes #discourse-comments element exists; throws if missing
findings.body: The IIFE immediately does document.getElementById('discourse-comments') and later comments.appendChild(iframe) without a null check. If the embedding page includes this script without a #discourse-comments div (a trivial integration mistake), the script throws a TypeError and the embed never renders, with no error message. A null check with a console warning would make integration failures diagnosable.

findings.title: Loading page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely, causing repeated job enqueues
findings.body: The loading view reloads the page every 30 seconds via setTimeout. Each reload hits EmbedController#best, which (while no TopicEmbed exists) enqueues another Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) every 30 seconds per viewing browser. TopicRetriever throttles actual fetches to once per 60s per URL for non-staff, but each reload still enqueues a job (jobs pile up in Sidekiq) and each request re-renders. For a popular embed whose source is slow or permanently failing, this creates a self-inflicted load amplification: N viewers → 2N jobs/minute. The reload loop should back off, or the controller should not enqueue a job when one is already pending/in-progress (e.g. check a Redis key set by RetrieveTopic).

findings.title: Embed route is defined before the catch-all topic routes, shadowing nothing but placed inconsistently; no rate limiting on the endpoint
findings.body: The route get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best' is placed after the topics/private-messages routes but before the 't/:id' topic routes. It does not conflict, but the endpoint is publicly accessible, performs a DB lookup and enqueues a job per request, and has no rate limiting at the Rack/Rails level (the only throttle is inside TopicRetriever for the fetch, not for the endpoint itself). An attacker can hammer /embed/best?embed_url=... to fill the Sidekiq queue with RetrieveTopic jobs (each of which does a Redis setnx and a DB exists? check). Rack::Attack or a controller-level rate limit should protect this endpoint.

findings.title: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative URLs, not other relative forms, and mishandles protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: absolutize_urls rewrites href/src only when they start_with?('/'). Relative URLs like 'images/foo.jpg' or '../foo' are left relative, so in the rendered post they resolve against the Discourse forum's origin instead of the source site — broken images/links. Protocol-relative URLs ('//cdn.example.com/x.jpg') start with '/' and are incorrectly rewritten to 'http://sourcehost//cdn.example.com/x.jpg' (double slash after host), producing a broken URL. The method should use URI.join(uri, href) to correctly resolve all relative forms, and skip absolute and protocol-relative URLs.

findings.title: PollFeed spec only tests execute gating; poll_feed itself (the actual feed parsing and import) is untested
findings.body: The spec only verifies that execute calls poll_feed when settings are present and doesn't when they're missing. The poll_feed method — which contains the actual logic (user lookup, SimpleRSS parsing, URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import loop) — has no tests. Given that poll_feed has known fragility (nil i.content, fetch errors, malformed feeds), tests should cover: successful import of items, skipping items with invalid URLs, behavior when the feed is unreachable, and behavior when embed_by_username doesn't exist. The require_dependency at line 2 also loads 'jobs/regular/process_post' which is unrelated to PollFeed (copy-paste error) and should be 'jobs/scheduled/poll_feed'.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options set to invalid value ALLOWALL
findings.body: response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL" — ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive (the spec defines only DENY and SAMEORIGIN; ALLOW-FROM is deprecated/unsupported). Browsers ignore invalid X-Frame-Options values, so this header provides no framing protection and gives a false sense of security. Since the embed is intended to be framed by the embeddable host, the correct approach is to omit X-Frame-Options (or use CSP frame-ancestors with the specific embeddable host), relying on the referer check — but the referer check itself is spoofable as noted. At minimum the invalid header should be removed or replaced with a CSP frame-ancestors directive listing SiteSetting.embeddable_host.

findings.title: PostRevisor#update_post ignores save failure, allowing silent data loss on revision
findings.body: update_post calls @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) and ignores the return value. If save fails (e.g. a DB-level error, or with validations enabled a validation failure), revise! still returns true and the caller (TopicEmbed.import) proceeds to update embed.content_sha1, marking the content as updated when it wasn't. This is a general data-integrity bug in PostRevisor affecting all revision paths, introduced/exposed by this PR's change to pass skip_validations through. The method should check the save result and raise or return false on failure so callers don't record success.

findings.title: import_remote passes unsanitized readability output to import which stores it as raw_html
findings.body: import_remote extracts doc.content via ruby-readability with a tag/attribute whitelist (div p code pre h1-h3 b em i strong a img; attributes href src). While this strips

findings.title: CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content can reintroduce HTML entities that alter stored markup
findings.body: content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) unescapes HTML entities in the feed content before it is stored as raw_html. If the feed contains <script>alert(1)</script> (escaped HTML, common in RSS content:encoded fields that are double-escaped), unescapeHTML converts it to literal <script>alert(1)</script>, which is then stored as raw_html and rendered unsanitized (see post.rb finding). This actively converts safe escaped content into executable HTML. The unescapeHTML call should be removed; if the feed double-escapes, the correct fix is to not unescape and let the raw_html sanitization (which should exist) handle it.

findings.title: Update test does not verify content_sha1 is updated or that unchanged content does not create a revision
findings.body: The 'Supports updating the post' test only checks that post.cooked matches /new contents/. It does not verify that the TopicEmbed.content_sha1 was updated (so future identical imports don't re-revise), nor that importing the same content twice does not create a new post revision (the should_revise? guard in PostRevisor). These are core behaviors of the import method (change detection via content_sha1) and should be asserted: after a second import with identical content, post.version should be unchanged; after import with new content, embed.content_sha1 should equal Digest::SHA1 of the new contents.

findings.title: update_column skips callbacks/updated_at and is not transactional with the revision
findings.body: embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) performs a direct SQL UPDATE outside any transaction wrapping the PostRevisor.revise! call. If the process crashes between revise! committing and update_column running, the embed retains the old sha1 and the next poll will re-revise the post (creating a spurious revision). Conversely if update_column runs but the revision transaction rolled back (it can't here since revise! is called first, but ordering matters), the sha1 would be wrong. The sha1 update should be inside the same transaction as the revision, or revise! should be wrapped with the update in a Topic.transaction block.

findings.title: Calling Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside TopicRetriever is wrong layering and can recurse/deadlock
findings.body: perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) directly (synchronously) when feed_polling_enabled is set, instead of enqueueing the job. This runs the entire feed poll (fetching and importing every item in the feed) inside the RetrieveTopic job, which was triggered by a single embed request. Consequences: (1) the RetrieveTopic job can run for a very long time (Sidekiq timeout), (2) it duplicates work — PollFeed is also scheduled hourly, so every embed request re-polls the entire feed, (3) if the feed contains the embed_url, this creates a nested import while the outer import for the same URL may also be in flight, hitting the race described in the TopicEmbed finding, and (4) it's a layering violation — jobs should enqueue other jobs (Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)) rather than instantiating and executing them inline. The correct behavior is Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed) or to not invoke PollFeed from here at all.

findings.title: skip_before_filter :check_xhr and :preload_json may not exist / are Rails-version dependent
findings.body: The controller skips check_xhr and preload_json before filters. If these filters are not defined on ApplicationController in all supported Rails versions (the Gemfile dual-boots Rails 3.2 and Rails 4), skip_before_filter raises ArgumentError ('no such filter') at load time, breaking the controller. The codebase uses skip_before_filter elsewhere, but the existence of check_xhr and preload_json should be verified for both boot modes; using skip_before_filter with `if:` or `unless:` guards, or skip_filter with raise: false (Rails 4.1+), would be safer. This is a potential boot failure on one of the supported Rails versions.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace-only change removes trailing newline at end of file
findings.body: The diff for this migration only removes trailing whitespace on line 2 and removes the final newline at end of file (line 33: 'end' with no trailing newline). This is an unrelated change to a historical migration that should not be modified (migrations are immutable once run in production). Removing the trailing newline and touching an already-shipped migration adds noise and risk (e.g. checksum-based migration verification in some setups) with no benefit. The file should be left unchanged.

findings.title: Missing trailing newline at end of file
findings.body: The file ends without a trailing newline (line 69 '}' with \ No newline at end of file). This is a minor style issue that can cause noisy diffs when the file is later edited (the last line appears modified). Not a functional problem but should be fixed for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

findings.title: Missing trailing newline at end of file
findings.body: The file ends without a trailing newline. Same minor consistency issue as other new files; should end with a newline.

findings.title: Missing trailing newline at end of file
findings.body: The file ends without a trailing newline. Minor consistency issue.

findings.title: Missing trailing newline at end of file
findings.body: The file ends without a trailing newline. Minor consistency issue.

findings.title: Referer host comparison does not handle www prefix, subdomains, or ports, causing legitimate embeds to be rejected
findings.body: URI(request.referer).host returns the host without port. If SiteSetting.embeddable_host is configured as 'eviltrout.com' but the embedding page is served from 'www.eviltrout.com', or the referer includes a non-default port (URI(...).host strips the port, so 'eviltrout.com:8080' yields host 'eviltrout.com' — actually that matches), the exact string comparison fails and the embed is rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Conversely if embeddable_host includes 'www.' it won't match the bare domain. The comparison should normalize both sides (strip leading 'www.', compare registrable domains or use a configured exact match with documentation). As written, the feature is brittle to common configuration variations and the failure mode (Discourse::InvalidAccess) is a 403 that breaks the embed with no diagnostic.

findings.title: topic_id_for_embed does not validate or normalize the embed_url before lookup
findings.body: TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) passes the raw param directly to a WHERE clause. The controller passes params[:embed_url] unvalidated. While SQL injection is prevented by ActiveRecord's parameter binding, the lookup is exact-string: 'http://example.com/page' and 'http://example.com/page/' or 'https://example.com/page' are treated as different embeds, so the same article embedded with different URL spellings creates duplicate topics (each triggering a separate fetch/import). The embed_url should be normalized (scheme/host lowercase, strip fragment, strip trailing slash, default ports) before lookup and storage to dedupe. This is both a data-integrity issue (duplicate topics) and a fetch-amplification issue.
